Text:
One single continuous photograph — no panels, grids, or split frames.
A photorealistic 2025 photograph of a single-storey suburban discount department store with a long flat-roofed frontage, a deep asphalt parking lot in front of the entrance and landscaping islands between the parking bays, shot from the parking lot towards the entrance.
Use the uploaded photo as the exact base composition. It shows this same place in an earlier year: first remove EVERY person, vehicle and bicycle already in it, so the lot and the frontage are bare, then populate them as specified below. Keep none of the earlier year's figures or traffic.

CONTINUITY
The same location 10 years later: same camera position, framing, building footprint, parking geometry, landscaping islands and neighbouring storefronts. Only historical content changes.

REDEVELOPED
The original building footprint and roofline are unchanged. The frontage is now subdivided into several separate tenant units, each with its own entrance, glazing and awning. The fascia has been resurfaced in fresh uniform cladding across the whole building and carries current tenant signage only — no earlier store name, outline, ghost lettering or mounting hardware survives anywhere on it. The pylon sign at the road carries a stack of current tenant panels.
The units now trading are Five Below, Retro Fitness, Burlington Coat Factory and Savers — one per bay, each with its own sign across its own unit, spelled exactly as given and no other wording.

SCENE
The place reads redeveloped — repurposed, practical, ordinary again.
The parking lot is half full — bays taken in loose clusters, whole rows empty.
Neighbouring units along the same frontage: tyre shop, thrift store, self-storage frontage, coffee kiosk.

VEHICLES
The vehicles are of the period — for example contractor pickups, modern crossovers, delivery vans, or anything else in keeping with the year. Nothing newer than the year of the photograph appears anywhere in frame.

PEOPLE
A scattering of shoppers is spread across the frontage, walking to and from the entrance and across the lot, each one doing something plainly ordinary.
Period clothing and grooming: trainers, phones held up, quilted gilets.
Among them: pointing something out in the window display, wheeling a shopping cart back across the lot, checking a receipt just outside the door — each only where it plausibly fits.
Every person is a different individual — no repeated face, build, pose or outfit.

PERIOD DETAILS
Store signage reading "SUITE ENTRANCE", "NOW OPEN", "FOR LEASE".
Period advertising and fittings: delivery bay markings, window graphics, charging bay markings.
Place each detail where it plausibly belongs — sidewalk, storefront, lot edge, under an overhang. If there is nowhere for one, leave it out; nothing stands in the roadway or a driving lane.
No other readable text appears anywhere in the image.

PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE
COLOUR photograph — digital — smartphone or mirrorless camera, wide dynamic range, clean detail.
Photorealistic — NOT black-and-white, no HDR.

PRIVACY
Blur every face and make every licence plate unreadable.
